text:
lucas: Heads-up: onboarding Calliope6b-hybrid (Llama/Gemma blend) into Dedicated. Ran int8 headwise fusion conversion and the summarization/qa evals show quality collapse after ~150 tokens — outputs become fragmented and embeddings drift. Short log + quick repro below.

priya: can you paste the eval command and a minimal failing sample?

lucas: repro:
```
./eval/run_eval.sh --model calliope6b-hybrid-int8h --suite summarization,qa --bs 16 --seed 13
```
Bad snippet: 
"""
System: Conversation context (long thread)
User: summarize the action items and owners
Expected: tidy bullets with owners Alice/Bob and next steps
Observed: scattered tokens, owner names garbled, repetition of fragments like "follow up with" 6x
"""

dana: did you compare with fp16 and int8 without headwise fusion? helps isolate whether fusion or quant is the problem.

lucas: fp16 and straight int8 per-channel (no headwise pack) match baseline. Drift only shows when we apply headwise-fused pack + our rotary-scaling optimization (we bake a per-head alpha).

marc: headwise fusion means we concatenated q/k/v per head into a packed buffer for better memory locality, and then applied asymmetric int8 quant with a per-row scale, right?

lucas: yes. converter flow: load weights -> headwise concat -> per-row abs-max scale -> quantize asymmetric int8 -> write header with head_stride meta and alpha param baked for rotary. Hypothesis: the rotary alpha we bake is interacting poorly with per-head scale zero-points causing phase drift in attention.

priya: interesting. Could also be tokenizer normalization mismatch for this model family. Calliope training used NFKC then a custom emoji cluster merge; our tokenizer does NFD by default which can shift token boundaries in long context and change kv-cache indexing. Have you diffed tokens for the failing sequence?

lucas: I did both. Short prefixes tokens match, but after ~120 tokens we see a unicode normalization divergence on a line with soft-hyphen + emoji, e.g.:
```
# fp16 tokens around split: ... 3432 78 9001 502 2
# int8h tokens around split:  ... 3432 78 9001 503 2  <- 502->503 shift after emoji cluster
```
So there's a token id bump plus the headwise fused int8 model shows a larger logit drift even on identical prefixes (we computed L2 on logits).

dana: can you paste the per-token logits diff check? small script you used?

lucas: quick script output (L2 norm over next-token logits for first 64 tokens):
```
fp16 vs int8 (no fusion): mean L2 2.1e-4
fp16 vs int8h (headwise fused): mean L2 8.9e-3  <-- flags
```

marc: L2 ~9e-3 is big. If the rotary alpha is baked with float rounding before quantization it could amplify phase error. Two-pronged theory: 1) rotary scaling baked per-head then quantized introduces small asymmetric bias in sine/cos basis for each head, 2) tokenizer normalization shift causes kv indices to move so drift compounds.

priya: action plan for triage: a) run int8h but disable alpha bake (keep alpha multiplicative in runtime as fp32) to see if quantization of alpha is the issue, b) run int8h but with tokenizer forced to NFKC+calliope-emoji to see if tokenization explains long-context flip.

lucas: running (a) now. runtime override:
```
export REDWOOD_RUNTIME_FLAGS=ROTARY_ALPHA_RUNTIME=1
./serve_local.sh --model calliope6b-hybrid-int8h --port 9133 --no-autobatch
```
ci-bot: deploy-check: port 9133 up, health ok, p95 92ms, queued eval job.

lucas: quick follow-up: disabling alpha-bake reduces L2 to ~3.2e-3 and summary coherence improves significantly (almost baseline for first 200 tokens). So alpha quantization is a major factor.

priya: good signal. For (b) tokenizer: run with forced normalizer:
```
export TOKENIZER_NORM=CALLIOPE_NFKC
./eval/run_eval.sh --model calliope6b-hybrid-int8h --suite summarization --seed 13
```

lucas: tokenizer forced run reduces the token id divergence (502->502) and removes the late-context shift for those samples. With both fixes (alpha-runtime + tokenizer normalize) outputs are near baseline. So two independent contributing factors.

marc: conclusions: i) avoid baking rotary alpha into int8 quantized weights — prefer runtime fp32 alpha or carefully quantize alpha with per-head symmetric scale that preserves sine/cos basis; ii) add converter fingerprinting for tokenizer normalizer (store expected normalization in model header) and fail conversion if runtime tokenizer mismatches.

priya: additional safety: add an eval guard that computes next-token softmax KL over first 64 tokens between reference fp16 and any new export, and fail onboarding if KL > 5e-3 on >5% of samples. Also add unit tests that include unicode edgecases (soft-hyphen, ZWJ emoji sequences).

lucas: I'll open PRs:
- converter: add --preserve-alpha flag and header field alpha_mode (BAKED|RUNTIME) + store tokenizer_norm fingerprint
- tests: add unicode+emoji long-thread samples to /eval/artifacts/calliope6b-hybrid/ and KL guard.

marc: I'll prototype safe-alpha quant scheme: quantize sine/cos table with per-head symmetric quantization and apply bias-correction during runtime to cancel z-point drift. If that doesn't help we keep alpha runtime-only. Perf hit estimate: ~1% p95.

dana: also log per-layer headwise quant scales in exporter and add a sanity check that no head scale differs >8x from median (large outliers likely numeric issues).

lucas: noted. Action items:
- lucas: PRs for converter flags + test artifacts + run baseline KL checks
- marc: prototype safe-alpha quant + perf run
- dana: add exporter head-scale outlier check and tokenizer_norm header validation

lucas: will drop artifacts and link PRs, thanks all :thumbsup:

ci-bot: ticket created: #ONB-2789 "Calliope6b-hybrid headwise-int8 rotary-alpha + tokenizer drift" assigned lucas/marc/priya, priority P2.
